title: Projects
text:
Here are some of my key projects that demonstrate my skills in data analytics, visualization, and business analysis.






Revenue Distribution





Units Sold Distribution





Units Sold vs Revenue (Under 10k)


Description: An end-to-end exploratory data analysis of 11,500 Apple sales transactions across 27 features, spanning 2022–2024. The project covers data cleaning, imputation, visualization, and business-driven insights across product categories, regions, sales channels, and customer segments.
Technologies Used: Python, Pandas, Matplotlib, Seaborn, Jupyter Notebooks
Key Highlights:

Cleaned and imputed missing data across storage, previous device OS, and customer rating columns
Built 15+ visualizations including distribution plots, heatmaps, correlation analysis, and revenue breakdowns
Identified that discounting does not drive volume — the 15% discount tier generates ~$427 less revenue per transaction with no compensating uplift in units sold
Analyzed return rates, customer ratings, and revenue by region, category, and sales channel

title: About Me
text:
Hi, I’m Thomas Primero! 👋
I’m a recent Business Analytics graduate from Boston University with a background in finance and operations. I enjoy building visualizations that tell a clear story and turning raw data into practical business solutions, whether that’s through analysis, modeling, or writing functions that make the work repeatable and scalable.

title: About Me
text:
Background
I started my career as an Operations Specialist at Charles Schwab, validating complex payroll and census datasets and automating workflows with Excel and VBA. I was good at it, but I kept finding myself more interested in the patterns behind the numbers than the numbers themselves. What did the data actually mean? What could it predict? That curiosity is what led me to Boston University.
At BU, I leaned into the investigative side of analytics; taking messy, real-world datasets and working through them end to end: cleaning, exploring, visualizing, and building solutions that actually mean something to a business. I graduated in May 2026 with a Master’s in Business Analytics, and that process of turning raw data into a clear answer is still what I enjoy most.

title: About Me
text:
What I Do
I specialize in:

Data Analytics: Using Python, SQL, and R for data processing and analysis
Machine Learning: Building predictive models and classification algorithms
Data Mining: Feature engineering, exploratory analysis, and uncovering patterns in complex datasets
Data Visualization: Creating interactive dashboards with Plotly and Tableau
Business Analysis: Writing reusable functions and building end-to-end analysis pipelines that translate data into actionable business recommendations

title: About Me
text:
Career Goals
I’m a recent graduate looking for a data analyst or data scientist role where I can do work that actually matters to a business. My operations background at Charles Schwab gives me a practical lens;I understand data quality, I’ve worked with and have seen how messy real datasets get, and I know how to communicate findings to people who aren’t data/payroll analysts.
I’m especially drawn to roles in marketing analytics, public sector research, or research-focused teams where thorough exploration directly shapes strategy — whether that’s in the private sector or public service.
